doc: Mission 2, STS-61, the first Hubble servicing mission (December 1993): 'Glasses for a telescope' (issue #46). (1) Five spacewalks, each a parts-in-order task against its own clock: the real parts of each outing and its real length [S-sts61-nasa], 35 h 28 min in all [S-hubble-sm1]. A spacewalk whose clock runs out is tried again. (2) The climax: the first sharp image, the player turns the correction until M100's stars snap to points, then NASA's real images of M100 before (WFPC1, 1993) and after (WFPC2) [S-m100-pia22913]. Our simplifications, said on screen: the order of the parts inside an outing, time run fast (each outing in about a minute), and the correction as a dial (in reality the optics of WFPC2 and COSTAR did it).

steps.houston: Spacewalk one. Open the equipment bay and swap in the two new Rate Sensing Units: the gyroscopes Hubble steers by.
Now the two electronic control units for the gyroscopes.
Last: the eight new fuse plugs. Then close the doors.
Spacewalk two. The old solar arrays come off: put the new ones on.
Spacewalk three. Slide out the old camera and slide in Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2: its optics carry the correction for the mirror.
Now the two new magnetometers, at the top of the telescope.
Spacewalk four. Out with the High-Speed Photometer, in with COSTAR: glasses for the other instruments.
And the co-processor for the flight computer: more memory, more speed.
Spacewalk five. Replace the Solar Array Drive Electronics.
Then the Goddard High Resolution Spectrograph's redundancy kit.
Last job: protective covers over the old magnetometers. Then home.

parts.name: Rate Sensing Units
parts.line: Two units with the gyroscopes that tell Hubble how it turns.

parts.name: Gyro control units
parts.line: Two electronic control units for the gyroscopes.

parts.name: Solar arrays
parts.line: New wings to turn sunlight into power.

parts.name: WFPC2 camera
parts.line: Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2, built to make up for the mirror's flaw.

parts.name: Magnetometers
parts.line: They feel the Earth's magnetic field, to know which way Hubble faces.

parts.name: COSTAR
parts.line: Corrective optics for the other instruments: Hubble's glasses.

parts.name: Co-processor
parts.line: For the flight computer: more memory and speed.

parts.name: Array drive electronics
parts.line: Solar Array Drive Electronics: they turn the wings toward the Sun.

parts.name: Spectrograph kit
parts.line: A redundancy kit for the Goddard High Resolution Spectrograph.

parts.name: Magnetometer covers
parts.line: Protective covers for the original magnetometers.

parts.name: Killa's lens cloth
parts.line: Killa wants to clean the lens. Nobody lets her.

wrong: Negative, that is not this step's part.
cloth: Killa, put the cloth away. Nobody is cleaning the mirror.

urgent.20: Twenty seconds left on this spacewalk. Keep going.
urgent.10: Ten seconds! Finish and get back to the airlock!

lost_sub: Back to the airlock. That is not how it went: the crew finished every spacewalk. Try this one again.

focus.title: The first image
focus.houston: Houston here. The first picture with the new camera is coming down. Turn the correction until the stars are points.
focus.note: Simplified: here you turn a dial; in space the optics of WFPC2 and COSTAR did it.
focus.win_sub: The galaxy M100 snapped into focus.
focus.caption: The galaxy M100, as Hubble really saw it: with the old camera in 1993, blurry from the mirror's flaw, and with WFPC2 after this mission, sharp.

facts.text: It took five back-to-back spacewalks totaling 35 hours and 28 minutes to complete Hubble's first servicing mission.
Instead of focusing light to a single point, Hubble's flawed mirror had many foci: its first images looked fuzzy.
